title_en: Ritz Hotel Co., Ltd. v. Shanghai Huangpu Lichi Leisure and Fitness Co., Ltd. — infringement dispute
ruling_gist_en: According to Article 52 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the permission of the trademark registrant constitutes infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark. Pursuant to Article 4 of the same Law, the provisions of this Law concerning trademarks on goods apply to service marks. Whether the accused infringing mark and the claimed registered trademark are similar shall be determined by a comprehensive assessment of the factors that play a primary identifying role, such as the overall appearance and main parts of the two marks, considering the distinctiveness and market reputation of the registered trademark, and comparing the sound, shape, and meaning of the words, the composition and color of the graphics, or the combination of elements such as words and graphics, thereby determining whether the two marks are likely to cause confusion among the relevant public. Similar services refer to services that are identical in terms of purpose, content, method, and target, or that the relevant public generally considers to have a specific connection and are likely to cause confusion. Accordingly, if a person, without the permission of the trademark registrant, uses a similar mark on services that are similar to those provided by the trademark registrant, and such use is likely to cause the relevant public to misidentify, confuse, or believe that there is a specific connection between the two, the act constitutes infringement of the exclusive right to use the registered trademark.

full_text_en:
The Ritz Hotel, Limited v. Shanghai Huangpu Lichi Leisure & Fitness Co., Ltd. — dispute over trademark infringement

[Ruling Summary]

Pursuant to Article 52 of the Trademark Law of the People's Republic of China, using a trademark that is identical or similar to a registered trademark on the same or similar goods without the authorization of the trademark registrant constitutes infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark. According to Article 4 of the same Law, the provisions of the Law concerning goods trademarks shall apply to service marks. In determining whether the accused infringing mark is similar to the registered trademark for which protection is sought, consideration shall be given to the distinctiveness and market recognition of the registered trademark, and a comprehensive assessment shall be made of the elements that serve as the primary identifying function of the two marks, including the pronunciation, shape, and meaning of the words, the composition and colors of the figures, or the combination of elements such as words and figures, comparing the two marks as a whole and their dominant parts, so as to conclude whether they are likely to cause confusion among the relevant public. Similar services refer to services that are identical in purpose, content, method, and target, or that the relevant public generally considers to have a specific connection and are likely to cause confusion. Accordingly, if a person, without the authorization of the trademark registrant, uses a similar mark on services that are similar to those provided by the trademark registrant, and such use is likely to cause the relevant public to mistake or confuse the services, or to believe that there is a specific connection between them, such conduct constitutes infringement of the exclusive right to use a registered trademark.

Plaintiff: The Ritz Hotel, Limited, domiciled at South Street, London W1K 1DF, England.
Authorized Representative: Franz-Josef KLEIN, Director of the Company.
Defendant: Shanghai Huangpu Lichi Leisure & Fitness Co., Ltd., domiciled at Dianchi Road, Huangpu District, Shanghai, People's Republic of China.
Legal Representative: Chen Xuhua, General Manager of the Company.

The plaintiff, The Ritz Hotel, Limited (hereinafter referred to as Ritz Company), filed a lawsuit with the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court against the defendant, Shanghai Huangpu Lichi Leisure & Fitness Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huangpu Lichi Company), regarding a trademark infringement dispute.

Plaintiff's Allegations: The plaintiff is a world-renowned hotel operating company. Its business name and principal trademark "RITZ" have a history of nearly one hundred years. The "RITZ" trademark has been registered in over 900 registrations across more than 100 countries and regions. In China, the plaintiff registered the "RITZ" trademark in Class 43 (hotels, restaurants, etc.) and Class 44 (beauty salons, etc.), with registration numbers 3098934 and 3098933, respectively. The defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, is a company primarily engaged in services such as public baths (including saunas) and massages, and it uses the trademark "RITS" in its business operations. The plaintiff contends that its registered trademark "RITZ" enjoys high reputation, and the defendant's use of the similar mark "RITS" in services similar to those covered by the plaintiff's registered trademark causes consumers to confuse the source of services, dilutes the recognition of the plaintiff's trademark among the relevant public, reduces the brand value of the plaintiff's trademark, and has caused significant economic losses to the plaintiff, thereby infringing the exclusive rights of the two aforementioned trademarks. Accordingly, the plaintiff requests the court to order the defendant to immediately cease using the "RITS" trademark, pay the plaintiff RMB 300,000 in economic damages, bear the plaintiff's attorney's fees and investigation costs incurred in stopping the defendant's infringing conduct, and also requests the court to impose a fine on the defendant for its infringement and to confiscate the infringing goods.

Defendant's Defense: First, the defendant uses "RITS" primarily in combination with the Chinese characters "丽池" or as a combination of text and graphics ("丽池RITS及图"). Viewed as a whole, the mark is not similar to the plaintiff's trademark and will not cause confusion. The plaintiff's "RITZ" trademark has never been used alone in China, and "RITZ" itself lacks distinctiveness and recognition, making confusion unlikely. Second, the services provided by the defendant are neither identical nor similar to the services covered by the plaintiff's trademark. The defendant primarily provides sauna and acupressure services, which are "services for entertainment or pastime," while the plaintiff's trademark covers "medical services" and "personal hygiene and beauty services"; the types and purposes of the services are clearly different. As for the complementary catering services provided by the defendant, they are not the defendant's main business and should not define the nature of the defendant's services. Third, the defendant used the disputed mark and applied for trademark registration first, thus enjoying prior rights to the mark. Fourth, the disputed mark used by the defendant was independently created by the defendant's affiliated company and has always been used in good faith. The distinctive services of "sauna and acupressure" provided by the defendant and its affiliated companies have become well-known to the relevant public in Shanghai, and the defendant has no intention to infringe. Therefore, the defendant has not infringed the plaintiff's rights and requests the court to dismiss the plaintiff's claims.

Facts Found by the Court at First Instance:

The plaintiff, Ritz Company, a British company established in 1896, obtained registration from the Trademark Office of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce of the People's Republic of China (hereinafter referred to as the China Trademark Office) for the following trademarks: International Registration No. G611405 "LE RITZ" trademark, and Chinese trademarks No. 3098933 and No. 3098934 for "RITZ". The International Registration No. G611405 is protected in China through territorial extension, covering services such as hotels, restaurants, sanatoriums, nursing homes, beauty and hair salons, with a validity period from December 9, 1993 to December 9, 2013. Trademark No. 3098933 covers services in Class 44: beauty salons, barber shops, nursing homes, and spa facilities, filed on February 20, 2002, with a validity period from May 21, 2005 to May 20, 2015. Trademark No. 3098934 covers services in Class 43: hotels, restaurants, restaurants with grill rooms, fast-food restaurants, tea rooms, cocktail party services, bars, and hotel reservations, filed on February 20, 2002, with a validity period from October 7, 2003 to October 6, 2013.

On November 9, 1998, the plaintiff, Ritz Company, entered into a Trademark License Agreement with a third party, The Ritz-Carlton Hotel Company, LLC (hereinafter referred to as Ritz-Carlton Company), authorizing Ritz-Carlton Company to use "RITZ" as part of the "RITZ-CARLTON" mark in certain regions, including China, either by itself or through sublicenses. On August 7, 2000, Ritz-Carlton Company obtained registration from the China Trademark Office for the "RITZ-CARLTON" trademark, covering services such as hotels, restaurants, fast-food restaurants, and bars. A third party, The Portman Ritz-Carlton, Shanghai, established in 1998, uses the "RITZ-CARLTON" mark in its business operations. According to its website, "The Portman Ritz-Carlton, Shanghai has been officially awarded the Platinum Five-Star Hotel by the China National Tourism Administration," and "this award is the highest level in China's tourism hotel industry, and The Portman Ritz-Carlton, Shanghai is one of only three Platinum Five-Star Hotels in the country and the only international luxury hotel in Shanghai to receive this honor." The Ritz-Carlton, Beijing Financial Street and The Ritz-Carlton, Beijing Jianguo Road also use the "RITZ-CARLTON" mark in their operations.

The plaintiff, Ritz Company, has also registered the "RITZ" trademark or word/word-and-design combinations containing "RITZ" in Australia, Canada, Greece, South Africa, Israel, Singapore, Japan, Germany, and other countries.

The plaintiff, Ritz Company, has taken enforcement actions in multiple countries and regions to protect its legitimate rights in the "RITZ" mark. In a domain name dispute with Croatian company Damir Kruzicevics concerning "ritz-hotel.com," the World Intellectual Property Organization Arbitration and Mediation Center ruled on January 16, 2006, to transfer the domain name "ritz-hotel.com" to the plaintiff. The "RITZ" trademark registered in Japan in Classes 23 and 42 was recognized as a well-known trademark in a Japanese court decision. In a "Notice of Order to Rectify" issued by the Chaoyang Branch of the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce on September 15, 2006, it was determined that a third party, the Lido Hotel Management Branch of Aode Real Estate Company, had infringed the plaintiff's registered trademark exclusive rights by using "HQRITZ" without authorization in its external publicity, and the company was ordered to rectify.

A third party, Xiamen Lijing Entertainment Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xiamen Lijing Company), established in 1993 with Zhou Tao as its legal representative, applied to the China Trademark Office on September 11, 2000, for registration of a word-and-design composite mark "丽池RITS及图," designating services including "providing accommodation, restaurants, beauty salons, barber shops, massage," etc. During the preliminary examination and publication period, the plaintiff, Ritz Company, filed an opposition against Xiamen Lijing Company's application for registration of "丽池RITS及图" based on its registered International Registration No. G611405 "LE RITZ" trademark. On November 21, 2005, the China Trademark Office issued a ruling: The opponent's (Ritz Company's) trademark consists of "LE" and "RITZ"; since "LE" is a French preposition, the main element of the trademark is "RITZ." The foreign language part of the opposed trademark, "RITS," is identical to the first three letters of "RITZ." Although the fourth letters differ—"S" and "Z"—the pronunciation is similar, making it difficult for consumers to distinguish the two trademarks. The services designated by both trademarks are essentially the same in terms of content, method, etc., and are identical or similar services. Therefore, the opposed trademark constitutes a similar trademark to the plaintiff's International Registration No. G611405 "LE RITZ" trademark used on identical or similar services, and the registration of the opposed trademark was refused. Xiamen Lijing Company, dissatisfied with the ruling, applied to the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on December 8, 2005, for a review, which is currently pending. Additionally, Xiamen Lijing Company obtained registration from the China Trademark Office in 2004 for the word trademark "丽池" in Class 43 and the "水纹" figurative trademark in Classes 43 and 44.

The defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, was established on November 18, 2004, with a registered capital of RMB 2,000,000 and a business scope of public baths and foot care. Due to its location near the Bund in Huangpu District, Shanghai, the defendant refers to itself as "Bund 81 Lichi Club." According to its promotional materials in Chinese and English, in addition to providing sauna, acupressure, massage, beauty, hairdressing, and foot therapy services, it also offers "free accommodation," "free unlimited breakfast, lunch, dinner, and supper." The defendant stated that Xiamen Lijing Company and the defendant are both directly or indirectly invested by third party Zhou Tao and are affiliated companies; the affiliated companies uniformly use the "Lichi Club" brand in their business, with the brand slogan "In the vast sea of saunas, Lichi leads; Lichi acupressure, nationally top-notch." In an article titled "Enjoying Summer at Grand Bathhouses" published in the "Night Shanghai" section of *Travel Times* on August 5, 2001, "Lichi Sauna" was referred to as "having the highest class." The "Lichi Club" was recognized by the China Best Chain Enterprise Selection Committee as "2007 China's Best Chain Brand" and "2007 China's Most Investable Chain Enterprise."

On October 18, 2007, the plaintiff, Ritz Company, conducted notarial preservation of the defendant's use of the "RITS" mark at its business premises located at No. 81-85 Dianchi Road, Shanghai. According to the notarial certificate, the defendant used the "RITS" mark in three ways: 1. Using "RITS" alone on slippers; 2. Using the composite mark "丽池RITS及图" on items such as bathrobes, towels, toothbrush packaging boxes, and tissue boxes; 3. Using combinations such as "RITS" with "丽池," "RITS UNION" with "丽池会所," or "RITS CLUB" with "丽池会所" on advertising boards, in-store signage, menus, drink lists, and service tags within the business premises. During the trial, the defendant stated that it had changed the "RITS UNION" on its exterior signage to "RI-STARSPA," which the plaintiff confirmed.

The plaintiff, Ritz Company, incurred expenses totaling RMB 14,275 for translation fees, travel expenses, etc., in investigating the defendant's conduct. At the hearing, the plaintiff stated that it would not claim attorney's fees from the defendant.

The above facts are supported by the relevant trademark registration certificates, domain name ruling, Japanese well-known trademark search documents, the "Notice of Order to Rectify" issued by the Chaoyang Branch of the Beijing Administration for Industry and Commerce, the Trademark License Agreement between the plaintiff and third party Ritz-Carlton Company, the ruling of the China Trademark Office, promotional materials, notarial certificates, and the statements of the plaintiff and defendant.

Issues in Dispute at First Instance:
1. Whether the mark used by the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, is similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark.
2. Whether the services covered by the defendant's mark are identical or similar to the services designated by the plaintiff's registered trademark.
3. Whether the defendant has prior rights to the disputed mark.
4. Whether the amount of damages claimed by the plaintiff has factual and legal basis.

Opinion of the Court at First Instance:

1. Regarding the First Issue: Similarity of Marks

According to Article 9, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Adjudication of Civil Trademark Disputes, a similar trademark means that, compared with the plaintiff's registered trademark, the shape, pronunciation, or meaning of the words, or the composition and colors of the figures, or the overall structure of the combination of elements, or the three-dimensional shape or color combination of the accused infringing trademark are similar, and such similarity is likely to cause the relevant public to mistake the source of the goods or to believe that the source is associated with the goods bearing the plaintiff's registered trademark. Article 10 of the same Interpretation provides that the determination of identical or similar trademarks shall be based on the general attention of the relevant public; both a global comparison of the trademarks and a comparison of the dominant parts shall be made; and the distinctiveness and recognition of the registered trademark for which protection is sought shall be considered.

In this case, comparing "RITS" with "RITZ": Both marks consist of four letters, with the first three letters identical and only the last letter different. Both marks are expressed in ordinary fonts and look similar. Their pronunciations are similar. Therefore, the "RITS" mark used by the defendant is similar to the plaintiff's "RITZ" trademark, likely to cause the relevant public to mistake the source of the services or to believe that the source is associated with the plaintiff's services.

Regarding the distinctiveness and recognition of the plaintiff's trademark: As found by the court, the plaintiff was established in 1896 and has used the "RITZ" mark for over a century. "RITZ" and marks containing "RITZ" have been registered in many countries and have been recognized as well-known trademarks in Japan.

In China, third parties such as The Portman Ritz-Carlton, Shanghai, The Ritz-Carlton, Beijing Financial Street, and The Ritz-Carlton, Beijing Jianguo Road all use the "RITZ-CARLTON" mark. The plaintiff stated that these hotels are authorized to use "RITZ-CARLTON" under the Trademark License Agreement between the plaintiff and Ritz-Carlton Company. According to the Agreement, the plaintiff authorized Ritz-Carlton Company to use "RITZ" as part of "RITZ-CARLTON" in certain regions, including China, either by itself or through sublicenses. After obtaining authorization, Ritz-Carlton Company registered the "RITZ-CARLTON" trademark in China, and subsequently, the aforementioned hotels used the mark. Based on these facts, the plaintiff's claim regarding authorization is supported. The use of "RITZ-CARLTON" by The Portman Ritz-Carlton, Shanghai, etc., originates from the plaintiff's and Ritz-Carlton Company's authorization. Due to the high recognition of these hotels in the industry, "RITZ," as part of their business marks, also enjoys high recognition and strong distinctiveness in China.

Given the high recognition and strong distinctiveness of the plaintiff's "RITZ" mark, and considering the location of the defendant's business premises and the content of its promotional materials (targeting high-end clientele, including both Chinese and foreign customers), the "RITS" element in the defendant's combined marks such as "RITS" with "丽池" and "丽池RITS及图" is likely to attract the attention of the relevant public and easily cause confusion or mistake. Therefore, the combined marks containing "RITS" are also similar to the plaintiff's "RITZ" trademark.

2. Regarding the Second Issue: Whether the Services Involved Are Identical or Similar

According to Article 11, Paragraph 2 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Trademark Dispute Cases, similar services refer to services that are identical in terms of purpose, content, method, and target, or that the relevant public generally considers to have a specific connection and are likely to cause confusion. First, the business scope of the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, includes public bathhouses and foot care, and it provides services such as sauna, acupressure, massage, beauty, hairdressing, and foot therapy in its business activities. The designated services of the plaintiff's trademark No. 3098933 are beauty salons, barbershops, sanatoriums, and spa sanatoriums under Class 44. From the general understanding of the relevant public, the above services of the defendant are essentially identical to the designated services of the plaintiff's trademark No. 3098933 in terms of service content and method, and thus constitute identical or similar services. The defendant's argument that the services are not similar because each party focuses on different aspects of services lacks legal basis and is not supported. Second, according to the defendant's promotional materials and its statements, it provides services such as catering and accommodation in its business activities. The designated services of the plaintiff's trademark No. 3098934 are hotels, restaurants, fast-food restaurants, etc. under Class 43. Obviously, the services provided by the defendant are identical to the designated services of the plaintiff's trademark. The defendant argued that current sauna establishments all provide ancillary catering services, and that this service is not the defendant's main business, so it cannot be used to determine the nature of the defendant's services. In this regard, the court of first instance held that the provision of catering and accommodation services by the defendant is an objective fact, and whether such services are the defendant's main business does not affect the determination of identity or similarity of services.

In summary, the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, used signs similar to the plaintiff's registered trademarks on services identical or similar to the designated services of the plaintiff's registered trademarks No. 3098933 and No. 3098934.

III. Regarding the third disputed issue, i.e., whether the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, enjoys prior rights in the disputed marks.

The defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, claimed that its affiliated company, the non-party Xiamen Lijing Company, had been using the "Lichi RITS and Device" mark since 2000, while the application dates for the plaintiff's trademark No. 3098933 and No. 3098934 were both 2002, which is after the defendant's use of the mark. Moreover, through the efforts of the defendant and its affiliated companies, the "Lichi Club" had developed distinctive features in sauna and acupressure services and had gained widespread acclaim from the media and the public, enjoying high recognition. Therefore, the defendant claimed it had prior rights.

The plaintiff, Leitz Company, argued that it had already registered the "LE RITZ" trademark as early as 1993 and had used the "RITZ" trademark in China since 1998. Therefore, the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, did not have prior use nor had it established prior rights.

Based on the facts found above, the plaintiff, Leitz Company, obtained the exclusive right to use the international trademark No. G611405 "LE RITZ," which was extended to China through international registration in 1993. The non-party The Portman Ritz-Carlton, Shanghai was established in 1998 and had been using the "RITZ-CARLTON" mark in its name and business activities since 1998. Such use originated from the authorization of the plaintiff and the non-party Ritz-Carlton Company. Therefore, although the plaintiff did not independently use the "RITZ" trademark in China, the non-party, authorized by the plaintiff, used the plaintiff's "RITZ" trademark as part of "RITZ-CARLTON" in China, which constitutes a form of use of the plaintiff's "RITZ" trademark.

The non-party, Xiamen Lijing Company, applied for registration of the "Lichi RITS and Device" mark in 2000, which is later than the registration of the plaintiff's "LE RITZ" trademark and the use of the "RITZ" trademark. Therefore, the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company's argument that its affiliated company used the mark first cannot be established, and its claim regarding prior rights is also not supported.

IV. Regarding the fourth disputed issue, i.e., whether the amount of damages claimed by the plaintiff, Leitz Company, has a factual and legal basis.

The plaintiff, Leitz Company, requested that the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, compensate it for economic losses of RMB 300,000 and bear the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff in stopping the defendant's infringement. The plaintiff stated that because it could not prove the losses it suffered due to the defendant's infringement or the defendant's illegal gains, it requested the court to determine the amount of damages at its discretion, taking into account factors such as the defendant's use of the "RITS" mark since its establishment, its knowing continuation of use despite the plaintiff's opposition to its combined trademark, and its evident bad faith.

The defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, insisted that it had not infringed and therefore should not pay damages. It argued that because the plaintiff, Leitz Company, did not independently use the "RITZ" trademark in China, there were no losses and thus no damages. Additionally, the defendant claimed that its mark was created by itself and had been used in good faith. Through the defendant's efforts, its "Lichi Club" had gained high recognition in sauna and acupressure services, and the contribution of the use of "RITS" in the mark to the defendant's profits was minimal. Furthermore, the plaintiff was aware of the defendant's conduct but only filed suit in 2008, which was evidently in bad faith. Even if infringement were established, the plaintiff could only claim damages for conduct occurring within two years prior to the date of filing the lawsuit.

The court of first instance held that the plaintiff, Leitz Company, is the registrant of trademarks No. 3098933 and No. 3098934 for "RITZ" and enjoys the exclusive right to use these two registered trademarks in accordance with the law. According to the Trademark Law of the PRC, the exclusive right to use a registered trademark is limited to the trademark as approved for registration and the goods as approved for use. Without the permission of the trademark registrant, using a trademark that is identical or similar to the registered trademark on the same or similar goods constitutes trademark infringement. As discussed above, the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, used a sign similar to the plaintiff's registered trademark "RITZ" on services identical or similar to the designated services of the plaintiff's two registered trademarks, constituting trademark infringement.

Regarding the amount of damages, given that it is difficult to determine the losses suffered by the plaintiff, Leitz Company, due to the infringement by the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, and the profits gained by the defendant from the infringement, the court, taking into account the recognition and distinctiveness of the plaintiff's trademark, the manner of use of the plaintiff's trademark in China, the reasonable expenses incurred by the plaintiff to stop the defendant's infringement, and the nature, duration, and consequences of the defendant's infringement, determined the amount of damages at its discretion as RMB 200,000. In determining the amount of damages, the court specifically considered the following factors: the defendant used "RITS" mainly in combination with "Lichi" or as "Lichi RITS and Device"; the places where the above "RITS" mark was used, except for signs, were mainly within the defendant's business premises; the defendant had already changed the foreign language text on its external sign and no longer used "RITSUNION"; the plaintiff was aware of the defendant's infringement from the time of the defendant's establishment but only filed a civil lawsuit against the defendant on March 13, 2008. According to Article 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Trademark Dispute Cases, the amount of damages for infringement shall be calculated retroactively for a period of two years from the date the plaintiff files the lawsuit with the court. That is, the calculation period for damages in this case is from March 13, 2006, to March 13, 2008.

In summary, the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, infringed the exclusive right to use the plaintiff's registered trademarks No. 3098933 and No. 3098934 for "RITZ" and shall bear civil liability for ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses. The plaintiff's request to impose a fine on the defendant and confiscate the infringing items is not within the scope of the defendant's civil liability and is therefore not supported. Accordingly, pursuant to Article 4, Paragraph 3, Article 51, Article 52, Paragraph 1, Article 56, Paragraphs 1 and 2 of the Trademark Law of the PRC, and Articles 8, 9, Paragraph 2, Articles 10, 11, Paragraph 2, Article 12, Article 16, Paragraph 2, Article 17, Paragraph 1, and Article 18 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Civil Trademark Dispute Cases, the Shanghai No. 2 Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment on April 21, 2008:

1. The defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, shall immediately cease using the "RITS" mark in its business activities;
2. The defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, shall compensate the plaintiff, Leitz Company, for economic losses of RMB 200,000 within 10 days from the effective date of this judgment;
3. The remaining claims of the plaintiff, Leitz Company, are dismissed.

The case acceptance fee is RMB 5,800, of which the plaintiff, Leitz Company, shall bear RMB 967, and the defendant, Huangpu Lichi Company, shall bear RMB 4,833.

Huangpu Lichi Company, dissatisfied with the first-instance judgment, appealed to the Shanghai High People's Court. The main grounds of appeal were: 1. There were procedural errors in the first instance, rendering the judgment unfair. 1.1 The opposition to the registration of the involved trademark was under reexamination, and this case should have been stayed. 1.2 If the opponent disagreed with the reexamination decision, it could still file an administrative lawsuit, so the civil judgment should not interfere with the administrative ruling. 2. The facts found in the first instance were unclear and the findings were erroneous. 2.1 The trademark used by the appellant was not identical or similar to the appellee's "LE RITZ" trademark and would not cause confusion or mistaken recognition among the relevant public. 2.2 The scope of services designated by the appellee's trademark did not directly cover the bathhouse, sauna club, and fitness acupressure services engaged in by the appellant. The first instance's determination that they were identical or similar was an expansive interpretation. Even if the appellant had used its own trademark improperly, that would be a matter for administrative penalties. 2.3 Even if the appellee had obtained the exclusive right to use the "LE RITZ" trademark through international registration extended to China in 1993, it had not used or authorized use in accordance with the law. The appellee authorized others to use the "RITZ-CARLTON" trademark, which is a different trademark from "RITZ" and "LE RITZ," and the rights holders are also different. 2.4 The appellee's application for trademark registration was later than the use and application for registration of the involved trademark by the appellant's affiliated company. The appellant's trademark had prior use, and the "Lichi Club" mark enjoyed high recognition in China, especially in Shanghai's sauna clubs, so the appellant had prior rights. 2.5 The appellee's complaint in the first instance bore only the signature of the attorney and was not stamped by the law firm, so it could not represent the appellee's lawsuit. 3. The first instance applied the law incorrectly and rendered an improper judgment. 3.1 The first instance should have stayed the proceedings and issued a civil judgment that interfered with the administrative ruling. 3.2 The first instance erred in finding that the appellant's use of the "RITS" mark infringed the appellee's "LE RITZ" trademark.

The appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, submitted the following five pieces of evidence:

1. A record of trademark No. G611405 (Class 42) issued by the China Trademark Office on May 20, 2008, to prove that the registrant and address of the disputed trademark No. G611405 "LE RITZ" do not match the appellee, Leitz Company.
2. A printed webpage of "Inquiry Process" to prove that trademark No. G611405 had undergone an international partial transfer on December 10, 2002, and the rights holder had changed.
3. A printed webpage of "Announcement of Trademark Cancellation" to prove that trademark No. G611405 was canceled on November 18, 2004, due to non-use for three consecutive years.
4. A certificate issued on June 10, 2008, by the non-party Xiamen Lijing Company, to prove that the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark used by the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, was authorized by Xiamen Lijing Company.
5. A newspaper excerpt to prove that experts had different views on this case.

The appellee, Leitz Company, argued that the first instance found facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and the trial procedure was lawful, and requested dismissal of the appeal and affirmation of the original judgment. The main reasons were: 1. The fact that the administrative procedure had not concluded did not affect the trial of this case. The administrative review is a review of trademark authorization, while this case is a determination of trademark infringement. Even if the outcome of the administrative case differs from this case, the parties can still file an administrative lawsuit, so the procedural law has provided sufficient remedies for the rights holder. 2. The first instance found facts clearly. 2.1 The appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, has no lawful prior rights, and the appellee's trademark is legally valid. The "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark used by the appellant has only passed preliminary examination and has not been registered, so it does not enjoy legal protection. A trademark that has passed preliminary examination has only procedural prior rights that can oppose later-filed trademark applications but does not enjoy prior rights under civil law. The appellant's use of the "RITS" mark was in bad faith and does not constitute lawful prior rights. 2.2 Although the appellee's "RITZ" trademark has not been used independently, the licensee's use of the "RITZ" trademark in the form of "RITZ-CARLTON" in commercial activities is one of the effective forms of use. 3. The first instance applied the law correctly. 3.1 The "RITS" mark used by the appellant is similar to the appellee's "RITZ" and "LE RITZ" trademarks. 3.2 The services provided by the appellant are identical or similar to the services designated by the appellee's trademark.

The appellee, Leitz Company, submitted two pieces of evidence:

1. A copy of the notice of change of name and address of the owner of international trademark No. G611405 issued by the World Intellectual Property Organization (WIPO) International Bureau on May 12, 2008, and a translation, to prove that the registration information for the owner and address of trademark No. G611405 was incorrect and has now been changed to the name and address of the appellee, Leitz Company.
2. A record of trademark No. G611405 (Class 42) issued by the China Trademark Office on July 2, 2008, to prove that the rights holder of the disputed trademark No. G611405 "LE RITZ" is the appellee, Leitz Company.

The Shanghai High People's Court conducted a cross-examination in accordance with the law. Regarding the evidence of the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, the appellee, Leitz Company, argued that evidence 1, 2, and 3 were not new evidence for the second instance; evidence 4 was new evidence for the second instance, and its authenticity was acknowledged; evidence 5 was not evidence, and if experts were to provide testimony, they should appear in court for questioning.

The appellate court held that evidence 3 submitted by the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, lacked a formation date and could not be proven to have been formed after the first-instance trial. Evidence 1 and 2 could have been provided by the appellant to the first-instance court during the first-instance period. Therefore, evidence 1, 2, and 3 did not fall within the scope of new evidence for the second instance as stipulated in Article 41, Item (2) of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Evidence in Civil Proceedings, and were thus not admitted. Even if the above evidence constituted new evidence for the second instance, since the appellee, Leitz Company, submitted contrary evidence during the second instance proving that the registrant of trademark No. G611405 "LE RITZ" was still the appellee, evidence 1 still could not be admitted. As for evidence 2 and 3, since the appellee had already provided a certificate from the China Trademark Office during the first instance proving the registration status of trademark No. G611405 "LE RITZ," these two pieces of evidence alone could not negate the validity of the certificate issued by the China Trademark Office, so evidence 2 and 3 were also not admissible. Evidence 4 was admitted because the appellee acknowledged its authenticity; this evidence can prove that the appellant was authorized by the non-party Xiamen Lijing Company to use the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark. Evidence 5 is a newspaper report of scholars' personal views on the first-instance judgment of this case and is not evidence capable of proving the facts of this case, so it does not fall within the scope of evidence as defined by Chinese law and is not admitted.

Regarding the evidence provided by the appellee, Leitz Company, the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, argued that evidence 1 was not new evidence for the second instance, and since no original was available, its authenticity could not be confirmed. Evidence 2 was submitted after the hearing and exceeded the time limit for evidence submission, so the appellant refused to cross-examine it.

The appellate court held that evidence 2 submitted by the appellee, Leitz Company, was formed after the second-instance trial and proved new facts that occurred after the second-instance trial, so it was new evidence for the second instance and was admitted. This evidence can prove that the appellee is the rights holder of trademark No. G611405. Evidence 1, although a copy, its content can be corroborated with evidence 2, so it was also admitted.

After the second instance, the Shanghai High People's Court confirmed the facts found in the first instance. It further found that the notarized certificate No. (2007) Jing Dong Zheng Nei Zi No. 8340 issued by the Dongcheng District Notary Public Office of Beijing recorded that the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, used the words "RITS UNION" and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on its external store signs; used the words "RITS CLUB," "RITS UNION," and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on internal plaques and signs; used the word "RITS" or "RITS CLUB" on hand tags; used the words "RITS SAUNA" and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on bathrobes; used the words "RITS CLUB" and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on tissue boxes, cap boxes, lighters, and cups; used the words "RITS (BUND) CLUB" on menus and drink lists; used the words "RITS (BUND) CLUB" and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on club business cards and consumption receipts; used the words "RITS CLUB," "RITS SAUNA CLUB," and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on director membership card member regulations and membership application forms; used the words "RITS UNION" on handbags; used the words "RITS Lichi" and the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on plastic bags; and used the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark on towels.

The Shanghai High People's Court held in the second instance:

In trademark infringement dispute cases, to determine whether the accused infringing mark is similar to the registered trademark for which protection is claimed, consideration should be given to the distinctiveness and market recognition of the registered trademark. The factors to be compared include the sound, shape, and meaning of the words, the composition and color of the design, or the combination of words and designs and other elements. A comprehensive assessment should be made of the overall appearance, main parts, and other key identifying elements to reach a conclusion as to whether the marks are likely to cause confusion among the relevant public.

The appellee, Ritz Company, was duly approved by the Trademark Office of the PRC to enjoy the "LE RITZ" trademark in Class 42 services, with Registration No. G611405, valid from December 9, 1993, to December 9, 2013, covering designated services including "hotels; restaurants; rest homes; sanatoriums; nursing rooms; social companionship; marriage agencies; beauty and hair salons; reservation of rooms for tourists, etc."; in Class 43 services, it enjoys the "RITZ" trademark, with Trademark Registration Certificate No. 3098934, valid from October 7, 2003, to October 6, 2013, covering designated services including "hotels; restaurants; restaurants with grills; fast-food restaurants; tea rooms; cocktail party services; bars; hotel reservations"; and in Class 44 services, it enjoys the "RITZ" trademark, with Trademark Registration Certificate No. 3098933, valid from May 21, 2005, to May 20, 2015, covering designated services including "beauty salons; barbershops; sanatoriums; spa resorts." The appellee has the exclusive right to use the aforesaid registered trademarks in the designated services and is entitled to prohibit others from using, without its permission, trademarks identical or similar to its registered trademarks in respect of identical or similar services.

The appellee's aforesaid registered "RITZ" and "LE RITZ" trademarks are capable of distinguishing the source of services and possess high distinctiveness. Moreover, through years of use by the appellee, the "RITZ" trademark has been registered in many countries worldwide and was once recognized as a well-known trademark by a Japanese court. Domestically, the appellee's "RITZ" trademark has also become known to the relevant public through the licensing of the "RITZ-CARLTON" trademark, which includes the wording "RITZ", to relevant luxury hotels.

In this case, the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company, in its business activities, not only used the words "RITS" or "RITS CLUB", "RITS UNION", "RITS SAUNA", "RITS Lichi" individually, but also used the mark containing the word "RITS", namely "RITS, Lichi and Device".

From the perspective of the similarity between the word "RITS" used by the appellant and the appellee's "RITZ" trademark: comparing the appellant's used word "RITS" with the appellee's trademark "RITZ", both are in uppercase English letters, with similar fonts, pronunciation, and overall structure; the first three letters are identical; and the last letters "S" and "Z" are a corresponding pair of voiceless and voiced consonants in English, with similar pronunciation. Therefore, conducting an isolated comparison based on the general attention of the relevant public, and considering the distinctiveness and reputation of the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark, the word "RITS" used by the appellant constitutes a similarity to the appellee's "RITZ" trademark.

From the perspective of the service categories in which the appellant uses the word "RITS" and the service categories for which the appellee's "RITZ" trademark is registered: the appellant's business scope includes gymnasiums, bathing and massage, foot massage, beauty services, hairdressing, prepared dishes (excluding delivery), and beverages. In its services such as sauna, acupressure, massage, beauty, hairdressing, foot therapy, and catering, the appellant uses the word "RITS" or combined marks including the word "RITS" on its services and related items. The services designated for the appellee's "RITZ" trademark include hotels, restaurants, fast-food restaurants, tea rooms, beauty salons, barbershops, spa resorts, etc. Since beauty, hairdressing, and spa resort services typically include various forms of acupressure, massage, and various bathing, hydrotherapy, and related catering services, it should be determined that both the appellant and the appellee provide services such as beauty, hairdressing, bathing and hydrotherapy-related services, and catering services to the public. Therefore, the purposes, contents, and methods of the services they provide are identical or similar. Moreover, based on the appellant's promotional materials and the relevant licensing of the appellee's "RITZ" trademark, both target high-end customers as their service recipients, so the recipients of their services are also identical or similar. Consequently, the services provided by the appellant constitute services identical or similar to those designated for the appellee's "RITZ" trademark.

The appellant's use of the words "RITS" or "RITS CLUB", "RITS UNION", "RITS SAUNA", "RITS Lichi" is likely to cause the relevant public to be confused between the identical or similar services provided by the appellant and those provided by the appellee, or to believe that there is a specific connection between them. Such acts have infringed upon the exclusive right to use the appellee's two "RITZ" registered trademarks.

At the same time, the appellant also used the mark "RITS, Lichi and Device" containing the word "RITS" in its business activities. Although the proportion of the word "RITS" in this combined mark is relatively small, the word, as an element with a strong identifying function in a trademark, is still the main factor distinguishing the source of services for the relevant public receiving relatively high-end services, especially foreign nationals. Since the word "RITS" is similar to the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark, and the appellant simultaneously uses words such as "RITS", "RITS CLUB", "RITS UNION", "RITS SAUNA", "RITS Lichi" in its business activities, it is evident that the appellant subjectively intends to borrow the goodwill of the appellee's "RITZ" trademark. Objectively, the relevant public is also likely to be confused about the source of services indicated by the appellant's "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark containing the word "RITS", or mistakenly believe that the appellant and the appellee have a specific connection. Therefore, the appellant's use of the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark containing the word "RITS" also infringes upon the exclusive right to use the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark.

In summary, the appellant's use of the word "RITS" and the use of the word "RITS" in the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark, in services identical or similar to those designated for the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark, constitutes infringement of the exclusive right to use the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark. The appellant shall bear civil liability for ceasing the infringement and compensating for losses.

Regarding the appellant's grounds for appeal that the first-instance trial was procedurally unlawful and the judgment was unfair: the mark "RITS, Lichi and Device" applied for registration by the third party, Xiamen Lijing Company, was objected to by the appellee based on its registered "LE RITZ" trademark. The Trademark Office ruled that it constituted a similar trademark and refused registration. Xiamen Lijing Company's disapproval of this ruling and application for review do not necessarily necessitate a stay of the civil proceedings in this case. This case is a civil dispute concerning whether the word "RITS" contained in the commercial signs used by the appellant infringes upon the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark. The third party's application for review of the Trademark Office's ruling pertains to the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark. The subjects of these two cases are not entirely identical, and the outcome of that administrative review case is not a legal prerequisite for the trial of this civil case. Even if the third party files an administrative lawsuit against the review decision, it does not affect the handling of this case. It was not improper for the first-instance court to have failed to stay the proceedings. The appellant's appeal ground that the first-instance trial was procedurally unlawful and that the civil judgment interfered with the administrative ruling is not supported.

Regarding the appellant's appeal ground that the first-instance court's findings of fact were unclear and erroneous: First, based on the foregoing facts, the word "RITS" used by the appellant and the relevant marks containing the word "RITS" constitute infringement upon the exclusive right to use the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark. As for whether the appellant's irregular use of its own trademark should be subject to administrative penalties, that is beyond the scope of this civil infringement case. However, as long as the appellant's irregular use of the signs infringes upon another's legally registered trademark right, it constitutes infringement and should bear corresponding civil liability. Second, the services designated for the appellee's trademark are identical or similar to the services provided by the appellant. Third, the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark enjoys high international reputation in the hotel service category. By authorizing several domestic luxury hotels to use the "RITZ-CARLTON" trademark which includes the words of the "RITZ" trademark, the appellee enables the high-end individuals, especially foreign nationals, receiving its services to identify the source of the services indicated by the words, thus this constitutes a method of licensing its trademark. Fourth, prior use of a sign does not necessarily create rights. An unregistered trademark that has been in use and has gained certain influence can only obtain relief by preventing others from preemptively registering it by improper means. Moreover, in this case, although the appellant's use of the word "RITS" in the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark predates the registration date of the appellee's "RITZ" trademark, the appellee had already obtained the exclusive right to use the "LE RITZ" trademark through international registration as early as December 1993. Since the main part of the appellee's "LE RITZ" trademark is identical to its "RITZ" trademark, and the word "RITS" used by the appellant is similar to the appellee's "RITZ" trademark, the appellant does not enjoy prior rights over the word "RITS" in identical or similar services. The appellant's claim of enjoying prior rights over the word "RITS" lacks factual and legal basis. As for the reputation of the appellant's "Lichi Club" sign, in this case, the appellant only provided evidence showing that "Lichi Club" has received honors, but failed to provide evidence proving that the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark it uses has gained certain reputation. Meanwhile, since the appellee's "RITZ" trademark was applied for and registered in 2002 and approved, the appellant has not applied to the Trademark Review and Adjudication Board of the State Administration for Industry and Commerce to revoke the "RITZ" trademark on the grounds that the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark has gained certain reputation through use. Therefore, the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark is legally valid. After the appellee's "RITZ" trademark was registered, the appellant's use of the word "RITS" and the use of the word "RITS" in the "RITS, Lichi and Device" mark, which is similar to the appellee's "RITZ" trademark, constitutes infringement upon the exclusive right to use the appellee's registered "RITZ" trademark. Finally, as for the issue of whether the appellee's complaint bearing only the lawyer's seal can represent the appellee in filing the lawsuit, according to Article 63, paragraphs 1 and 2 of the General Principles of Civil Law of the PRC, a legal person may perform civil juristic acts through an agent. An agent performs civil juristic acts in the principal's name within the scope of the agency authority. The principal bears civil liability for the agent's acts of agency. In this case, the appellee authorized lawyers Meng Ting and Zhao Tianjuan on October 31, 2007, to participate in all litigation procedures related to trademark infringement, including filing the lawsuit on its behalf, signing any relevant legal documents (including the complaint), etc. Furthermore, the Beijing Branch of Lehman, Lee & Xu also issued a law firm letter confirming the aforementioned agency relationship. Therefore, the act of the two lawyers signing and sealing the complaint against the appellant on December 25, 2007, is an act of agency in filing the lawsuit on behalf of the appellee and has legal effect. The appellant's appeal ground that the first-instance court's findings of fact were unclear and erroneous is not supported.

Regarding the appellant's appeal ground that the first-instance court erred in applying the law and made an improper judgment: the issues of whether this case should have been stayed and whether the appellant's use of the word "RITS" constitutes similarity to the main part "RITZ" of the appellee's "LE RITZ" trademark have been detailed above. Therefore, the appellant's appeal ground that the first-instance court erred in applying the law and made an improper judgment is not supported.

In conclusion, the appellant's appeal requests and grounds lack factual and legal basis and should be dismissed. Accordingly, the Shanghai High People's Court, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) and Article 158 of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC, on July 22, 2008, rendered the following judgment:

The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed.

The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 4,300 shall be borne by the appellant, Huangpu Lichi Company.

This judgment is final.
